A waiver with approved_by 'research' exempts nothing. Without such a mechanism a CLI-only feature row would make --phase build unpassable.

coverage.features is stricter than the one-line task. Following references/10-gates.md GT-17 and 06-build.md BD-06, a feature also needs a visible heading and, unless its status is planned, a visible proof marker (data-proof, data-ledger or data-source). Two further rules: the status label must be visible with text, and when routes.json exists, an FR id not mapped to any route fails (CT-13), with the routes where it was found as evidence. Visibility is checked at every profile viewport.

coverage.placeholders checks more than the task's list (TODO, FIXME, lorem, TBD, [YOUR ...], xxx). Following GT-17 it also flags unrendered templates ({{x}} and ${x}, the FD13-F25 deck bug), example.com/org/net, John/Jane Doe, Acme and 'coming soon' stubs. Following the XRPL ui-audit precedent (FD13-F18) it flags broken values: NaN, [object Object], Invalid Date, and an element whose whole text is undefined or null. Text inside code, pre, kbd, samp and var elements is exempt.

coverage.nevershow scans more than rendered text, title and meta. It also covers hidden DOM text, text attributes (alt, title, aria-label, aria-description, aria-roledescription, aria-valuetext, placeholder, value) and application/json and ld+json data scripts, because all of these are published with the page. Evidence names the entry id, class, until date, route, viewport and place, never the matched text, so the gate report does not carry the private string. An entry that cannot be checked (invalid regex, bad date) fails the gate. A configured never-show file that is missing makes the gate skip, and so does no file configured at all.

coverage.metrics, interpretation: data-ledger must be on the data-metric element itself, and its row must be verified or backed (Hedera's vocabulary is mapped per FD13-F10). data-source with data-as-of is also accepted from the nearest enclosing data region ([data-source] and [data-as-of] ancestors, as recording.g13 describes), not only from the element itself. A 'stat-like figure' is visible, unmarked text outside code and time elements that holds a digit and is dominated by the figure: at most 3 words, or at least 40% digits and figure symbols. It must also not be a date, time, version, ordinal, step marker, page count or hash. Finally, it is either styled as a stat (font size at least 18 px and at least 1.25 times the body size) or carries a claim unit (%, a currency, x, k/M/B/bn/T, bp, or a ticker after the number).

Viewports: those named desktop and mobile, else all except 'reflow'. With no sponsor in the brief or the profile, the sponsor clause is not applied and the detail says so. deviations: Contrast pairs are declared in each colour token's usage text, because CONTRACTS 6.2 and assets/schemas/tokens.schema.json have no pairs field (additionalProperties false). A pair is the token names after on, over or against, joined by commas, and, or, slash, as in 05-tokens.md's own example 'secondary text, 4.5:1 or more on bg'. Names also declare pairs: on-<x> on <x>, <x>-foreground on <x>, foreground on background. The kind comes from the words before 'on': large is 3:1, text 4.5:1, a UI part (border, ring, focus, icon, input, chart) 3:1, a surface needs a 1.1:1 step in dark themes only, decoration has no minimum, and anything unknown counts as text. An explicit ratio in the usage can raise the minimum but never lower it. Two cases fail the gate: a text or UI colour that names no ground, and a ground name shaped like a token that matches no token (a typo would otherwise drop the pair silently). Suggested contract extension, for the owners of CONTRACTS.md and the schema: color.pairs [{fg, bg, kind}].

The leak gate scans more than built CSS and HTML. It always scans the source tree (JS, TS, JSX, TSX, CSS, HTML, Vue, Svelte, package.json), because FE-07's proof runs with no --serve. There it also flags missing @theme resets, colour, gradient and blur literals in plain CSS and inline styles (TK-05), and font packages in package.json. In built mode it also reads JS bundles (an SPA's class strings live there), default theme variables in built CSS (any of 26 palettes times 11 shades plus black and white, Tailwind's default shadows, radii, blurs and eases, and its 150ms or cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) transition), and font files named inter-* or geist-*. Tailwind-only checks are skipped when Tailwind is not detected (10-gates.md). Excluded: tests, the design folder, generated token CSS, venvs and framework caches. Geist or Inter imports pass when tokens.json declares that family.

CSS naming uses Tailwind's own namespace names (--color-<token>, --font-display/body/mono, --text-<style> with the --line-height, --font-weight and --letter-spacing sub-properties, --spacing-*, --radius-*, --shadow-*, --ease-*), plus --duration-* outside Tailwind. The @theme block therefore declares the base values under the same names, and the theme blocks, unlayered, override them at runtime. A numeric spacing name such as space-4 replaces Tailwind's p-4 step. The file also emits @font-face rules (URLs relative to the CSS file; --font-face no turns them off) and one .type-<style> class per type style (tabular-nums on data groups), as a bounded vocabulary per FD05-F13. Themes: the base (light if declared, else the first theme) sits on :root; the others go on :root[data-theme=<id>]; the first dark theme also gets .dark and a @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-theme]) block (--dark-media no turns it off).

The CSS path is <design>/tokens.css by default (TK-01), and --css <file> writes it elsewhere, for example FE-07's {ui_root}/src/styles. Each generated file carries a header with the tokens path, a sha256 of the canonical JSON and the build options. tokens.valid finds generated CSS under --root by that header and regenerates both views to compare them (line endings ignored): it fails on stale, hand-edited or missing views, and requires at least one generated CSS file. build refuses to overwrite a file it did not generate unless --force; the mirror's README is checked before anything is written.

tokens.valid checks more than the task list. It covers TK-02 (colour values must be hex, rgb() or oklch(); var(), color-mix(), relative colours and named colours fail; non-colour values may not use var(), color-mix() or currentColor) and TK-07 (oklch outside sRGB fails when its OKLab distance after clipping exceeds 0.002; this catches Tailwind blue-500 and indigo-500). TK-12: every font file needs a role; the mono family must be monospaced and used by a group. TK-14: font and licence files must exist and be non-empty. TK-17: tabular figures are read with opentype.js; data faces are the mono role, groups named for data, and the body face when neither exists. A mono face with no file counts as tabular by construction. A body system face that must show numbers fails, with the fix: add a mono role or self-host the face. TK-20 motion: an ease-out-shaped curve is required; ease-in, Tailwind's default curve, bounce and 'all' fail; durations must fit role budgets (press 160, tooltip 200, dropdown 250, modal 300, drawer or sheet 500, other UI 300); explanatory animations are exempt when the usage says so. TK-21: em dashes fail. Counts are reported, not gated (TK-03).

opentype.js 2.0.0 cannot read WOFF2, so tokens.mjs extracts the tables itself: brotli through node:zlib, the UIntBase128 table directory, transformed glyf and loca dropped, a transformed hmtx rebuilt. WOFF1 and SFNT files go through the same path. opentype.js then parses a reduced OpenType file (cmap, head, hhea, hmtx, maxp, name, OS/2, post, GSUB, CFF/CFF2, fvar, with stub glyf and loca). The opentype.js import carries a @ts-ignore because the package ships no type declarations.

palette: Leonardo 1.1.0 runs with OKLCH interpolation and HEX output. lib/color re-measures each value; a value below its target is moved along OKLCH lightness (hue kept, chroma cut only to stay in gamut) until it meets the target, then written as oklch(). Leonardo lands up to about 0.02 below target (measured 2.998, 4.493, 6.988), and its OKLCH output rounds every channel to an integer. Its own BackgroundColor triggers a `colorspace` deprecation console.warn on every Theme; tokens.mjs filters that one and passes any other warning through. Leonardo's types demand a BackgroundColor, so the runtime-supported CSS-string ground is passed through an any cast. Candidates are named <name>-<ratio> (brand-4-5) and their usage names the ground token, so pasted candidates are picked up by tokens.contrast (tested). With no --ground, the grounds come from tokens.json per theme (--ground-token, default bg).

Claude Design mirror (--mirror <dir>): writes <dir>/project/tokens.json, README.md and fonts/, following the Design System type's SKILL.md (release 1790818940-93cf, read with the Artifact tool's type description). It is list-shaped and puts the base theme first. Names are unique across families: non-colour names are their CSS variable names without --; a collision is a usage error. Families are full stacks, keyed by role. Lengths are px, rem, em or % (clamp() becomes its upper bound; other values are dropped and listed in the README). Motion is left out, because the type says '(not motion)', and appears in the README instead. Fonts whose licence names FFL or Fontshare are not copied (FD16-F12). project/design-system.json (a time-stamped index) and the cover component are not written: they belong to the publish step, and the type's cover.md could not be read without creating an artifact.
